Write me a 3 paragraph story about a tiger who learns to cook biryani
4:51 AM

Bagha was a young tiger in the hills of Ranthambore who had grown bored of raw dinners. One winter afternoon, a picnic group left behind a steel dabba, and the smell that rose from it made his whiskers tremble. It was biryani, and after one lick of the lid he made up his mind: he would cook it himself, no matter how long it took.

His teacher turned out to be Meena Tai, a retired cook who lived at the forest's edge and was far too old to be scared of anything. She made him wash his paws, then showed him how to soak the rice, brown the onions slowly and layer everything with saffron milk. Bagha was hopeless at first. He ate the marinated meat before it reached the pot, knocked over the salt with his tail and lifted the lid every two minutes until Meena Tai rapped his nose with a ladle. "Biryani needs patience, not claws," she told him.

So he learned to wait. On the seventh try he sealed the pot with dough, sat beside the fire and did not peek even once. When the lid finally came off, the steam carried cardamom and mint across the whole jungle, and the deer, the peacocks and one very suspicious sloth bear crept closer. Bagha served everyone on sal leaves, kept the smallest plate for himself, and found that a meal shared tasted better than any he had ever hunted.
